messages.author: 44c03a0165efd08f
messages.subject: Amplitude adjustment by frequency
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to create artificial traffic noise by creating a white noise wave file and then adjusting the amplitude of different frequencies to match the amplitude modulation of some basic traffic noise wav files (i.e. loud low frequency and quieter mid frequency and no high frequency). However, I'm not certain if this is possible in seewave. I know you can apply an amplitude envelope to a different wav file, but I don't want the temporal modulations.  What I'd really like to do is to take the output of ama and apply that curve to my white noise wave file.  Is this possible?

I've been thinking about resampling a white noise matrix, using the amplitude (0 through 1) from the ama as a probability of sampling. But I'm not quite clear on what the units of a sound matrix are.

I've also considered removing the amplitude modulation over time with rmam() and then mapping that envelope onto my white noise (still not quite what I want), but I'm getting an error when I use rmam on my noise Wave, as well as on a bird song Wave, but not when I follow the rmam example withe the synthesized file. Any ideas?

library(seewave)
library(tuneR)
> n <- readWave("./noise.wav", from=60, to=80, units="seconds")
> fee <- readWave("./song060.wav")
> rmam(n,f=44100)
Error in wave/Mod(hilbert(wave, f = f)) :
  non-numeric argument to binary operator
> rmam(fee,f=44100)
Error in wave/Mod(hilbert(wave, f = f)) :
  non-numeric argument to binary operator

Thanks!

Steffi

messages.author: 875f7ee6903447f7
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Amplitude adjustment by frequency
parts:
Steffi wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I'm trying to create artificial traffic noise by creating a white noise
> wave file and then adjusting the amplitude of different frequencies to
> match the amplitude modulation of some basic traffic noise wav files
> (i.e. loud low frequency and quieter mid frequency and no high
> frequency).

In order to do that you need filters and EQs. There is a package in R
called "signal" (mainly ports from Matlab/Octave) which does a lot of
different filterings, but if you want EQs you need to program
yourself... and that's not fun!

I think there is a simple and effective way to to do the job without
leaving R: you can you use SoX from R by system() calls . SoX does
everything you need at the best: filters, EQ, resampling (actually one
of the best resampling along with the iZotope RX and the Weiss
Saracon). By the way SoX is available for Linux/Unix/Mac/Win systems, so
no problem!

Best Wishes
Pietro Coretto

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Amplitude adjustment by frequency
parts:
Hi Steffi,

Regarding the use or rmam(), there is indeed a small bug concerning
the input object. Just do this to run it correctly:

r.noam <- rmam(n@left,f=44100)

Best regards,

Jerome

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Amplitude adjustment by frequency
parts:
Hello again,

SoX does indeed a lot of stuff that you can call from R.

You may also try to use the argument 'custom' of the function fir().

Generate your white noise and then apply a specific FIR filter with a
spectrum defined in 'custom'. See the two last examples of the
function fir().

HTH

Jerome
